content: Cypress Spurge is a plant belonging to the genus Euphorbia, which is indigenous to Europe and has been introduced to North America. It propagates through both seeds and an extensive, well-developed underground root system. The plant typically grows to a height ranging from 10 to 80 centimeters. It can be readily identified by its small, linear leaves, which measure approximately 2 to 4 centimeters in length and 1 to 2 millimeters in width. When the leaves are broken, they exude a milky sap. The plant also features petal-like bracts that are usually greenish-yellow in color. The milky sap produced by the plant is toxic and can cause skin irritation upon contact. Due to its invasive nature, Cypress Spurge is classified as a noxious weed in various regions, including the state of Colorado.
